newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/AT&T busy as stock slumps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/AT&T busy as stock slumps.

text.p: Several call options on AT&T Corp were active on Tuesday as the stock tumbled after a profit warning from the telecommunications giant.
The company's announcement early Tuesday that third and fourth quarter earnings could fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates touched off a string of rating downgrades by Wall Street firms.
By late trading, AT&T shares were down 5-3/4 at 51-1/2, a quarter-point above the session low. Consolidated volume topped 17 million shares.
The AT&T October 55 call traded about 7,100 contracts. It dropped 2-1/2 to 3/8 and had open interest of about 4,100.
The January 1997 55 call was the second most active AT&T call, with 1,925 contracts changing hands. It was down 2-9/16 at 1-9/16. Its open interest was about 5,175.
Other busy calls included the October 50, October 60, November 50 and 55.
On the put side, the October 50, up 11/16 at 13/16, traded nearly 2,300 contracts. It had open interest of 5,300.
The October 55 put and January 50 put each traded nearly 700 contracts.
Traders said the AT&T activity was both ways, with buying and selling seen in both calls and puts.
In other activity, the Safeway Inc December 37-1/2 call traded 10,500 contracts on the American Stock Exchange. On the Chicago Board Options Exchange, the contract traded five.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said an investor bought those Safeway calls at 4-1/2 when the stock was at 40-7/8 in early trade.
The trade was effected in two blocks, one of 9,999 contracts and one of 501. The option's open interest was about 450.
By Tuesday afternoon, the stock was up 1/2 at 41-1/4.
Another big trade was spotted in the MedPartners Inc March 1997 22-1/2 call, which traded 12,600 contracts. Its open interest was 20. The option traded at 2-3/4.
The volume crossed in several blocks, the largest of which was 5,300 contracts.
